docs.text: Are you a #GreatLakes #InvasiveSpecies researcher who wants to contribute to #AIS knowedge in the region? The #GLANSIS team requests your expertise for our first Grand Review of species profiles and risk assessments! Please reach out to Program Manager Rochelle Sturtevant, and share w/ your network!

The GLANSIS team's paper about Top 10 Great Lakes invaders has gotten a lot of press -- and you won't want to miss this version from .bsky.social which includes some very cool invasion timelines for the region's Most Unwanted: .bsky.social

Next week (2/24-2/28) is #NationalInvasiveSpeciesAwarenessWeek! Stay tuned as we feature content from #GLANSIS: a database hosting maps, ID, ecology, management, control, risk info, and more for 180+ #AIS in the #GreatLakes region. Learn more here: #InvSpWk #NISAW

….I’ll be honest, y’all, it’s tough to be my team’s comms specialist right now: I would truly love to spend all my time telling you about our amazing work at #GLANSIS and how we can protect our Great Lakes from invasive species, but current events are making even bigger threats apparent. 🫠

For #NationalInvasiveSpeciesAwarenessWeek (2/24-2/28), we’re featuring a #GLANSIS animated video series about #GreatLakes #InvasiveSpecies, ft. invasive carp, sea lamprey, mussels, ballast water invaders, + more, and how regional partners work together to stop them. Stay tuned! #NISAW

Bringing back some of the #GLANSIS team's greatest for #NationalInvasiveSpeciesAwarenessWeek: here's some great coverage of last year's landmark paper on the top 10 most impactful #GreatLakes #AIS! #NISAW

GLANSIS is run by a very small team that relies on ongoing partnerships with NOAA, Sea Grant, USGS, EPA, and more to do our work. Other major partners include the Cooperative Institute for Great Lakes Research, the Great Lakes Panel on ANS, and researchers at universities throughout the basin...

Today we're highlighting #GLANSIS to explore data on #GreatLakes #AquaticInvasiveSpecies! From species profiles to risk assessments to map data, GLANSIS makes historical data + cutting-edge research on #AIS available to scientists + the public.

Curious about which #GreatLakes #AIS have the most severe or wide-ranging impacts across the basin? Check out this paper from MISG's #GLANSIS team about the top 10 aquatic invaders in our region! #NISAW
Boosting again — come help the #GLANSIS team review our #GreatLakes #AquaticInvasiveSpecies risk assessments and species profiles for #AIS (and get paid for doing so!)
Do you have #GreatLakes #AIS data you’d like to share? Contact the #GLANSIS team to do so -- you can also direct us to additional resources or contribute to our peer review process! #InvSpWk #NISAW

One new #GLANSIS feature is a HUC8 watershed lookup that allows users to find and generate a printable map of their own #GreatLakes watershed -- a great tool for place-based learning! Explore the Huc8 Lookup tool at the link: www.glerl.noaa.gov/glansis/HUC8...
#GLANSIS got a facelift, go check it out! My whole team will be at #IAGLR26, so if you want to talk #GreatLakes invasive species data and where to host it, come find us in person in Winnipeg!

#GLANSIS is a Great Lakes-specific hub of the USGS NAS database, and has data-sharing agreements with #MISIN, #EDDMapS, #iMapInvasives, and more to track #AIS in the #GreatLakes basin. Explore GLANSIS for yourself here: #InvSpWk #NISAW

Exciting news: the #GLANSIS database has a new look! The Great Lakes Aquatic Nonindigenous Species Information System has the same functionality #AIS researchers know and love, with improved navigation and new features for scientists + educators. Check it out here: www.glerl.noaa.gov/glansis/

The #GLANSIS team will be attending and presenting at #IAGLR26 hosted by .bsky.social in Winnipeg, Manitoba in late May -- be sure to attend our session #19 on #InvasiveSpecies and come chat with us at the poster session. We'd love to share more of what we've been up to! #GreatLakes #scicomm

The #GLANSIS Risk Assessment Clearinghouse lets users access and compare #GreatLakes #AIS risk literature, including assessments, methods and results, from collaborators in the region. Learn more at the link: #InvSpWk #NISAW

Without our many federal, state, cooperative institute, and university partnerships, it would be impossible for the #GLANSIS team to fulfill our mission to provide the best possible invasive species data to scientists, environmental managers, legislators, and the public.

Another new resource is the #GLANSIS social science data hub, a repository of project results, final reports, and anonymized datasets on #GreatLakes social science projects available for secondary analysis. We're always looking for more data to add! www.glerl.noaa.gov/glansis/soci...
Had a nice chat with the Milwaukee Journal Sentinel this week about the #GLANSIS team’s recent Top 10 paper and the impacts of #InvasiveSpecies in the #GreatLakes! www.jsonline.com/story/news/l...

The #GLANSIS program was recently recognized in a Presidential Memorandum for our work protecting the #GreatLakes from #InvasiveCarp. Here's a 🧵 showcasing our species profiles + highlighting our partners who make the work of stopping Great Lakes AIS possible... www.whitehouse.gov/presidential...
#GLANSIS is in the news again! Check out this article on our Top 10 #GreatLakes #InvasiveSpecies paper from Great Lakes Echo: greatlakesecho.org/2024/10/07/s...

Interested in #GreatLakes #ParticipatoryScience? Join the NOAA #GLANSIS team and researchers at George Mason and collect invasive #MysterySnails! 🐌Scientists need your help collecting them to research their genetics + parasites. Learn more here: glerl.noaa.gov/glansis/contributeSnails.html 🧪
